title: A City Simulator, Opened Up parameters
$comment: Every default below was read from the vendored micropolisJS source at commit f13a1624 and matches it exactly. A default that disagrees with the engine is the worst possible bug in this sandbox, because the sandbox exists to show what the engine's defaults are. Slider granularity is x-step, never multipleOf - see the note in bathtub's schema for why. Property order is the panel's reading order: which layer to watch first (the simulation transport sits above it), then the two rules the sandbox leads with, then the other rules, then the run.

layer.title: Layer over the city
layer.description: Which internal layer to draw over the city, tile for tile. 'none' follows the rotation, so the overlay shows whichever layer the cycle most recently wrote. All fifteen are drawn small in the rail regardless; click one there to pin it.

crime_base.title: Crime base
crime_base.description: The crime rule is: crime = 128 - land value + population density - police. This is the 128. It's how much crime a place has before anything about the place is taken into account; the other terms adjust it. Nothing in the engine derived it and no data was fitted to produce it. Moving it changes the whole crime map at once, and population falls with it, because low land value raises crime and high crime lowers land value, and the engine links the two on purpose.

crime_land_value_weight.title: Weight on land value
crime_land_value_weight.description: How strongly low land value is taken to produce crime. The engine's value is 1, so one point of land value cancels one point of crime. At 0 the model stops connecting land value to crime at all, and the rest of the simulation carries on unchanged.

crime_police_weight.title: Weight on police
crime_police_weight.description: How strongly police presence reduces crime. The engine's value is 1. Police cover is on a 0 to 1000 scale and crime on 0 to 250, so a station at full strength doesn't reduce crime, it removes it. Policing here has no diminishing return, no displacement and no upper limit.

land_value_centre_base.title: Land value at the center
land_value_centre_base.description: The value of land at the city center, before distance is subtracted. The engine's 34 is shifted left twice (multiplied by four) in the code, so the real ceiling is 136. Raising this raises the whole land value surface without changing its shape.

land_value_distance_divisor.title: Distance divisor
land_value_distance_divisor.description: The land value rule is: land value = 34 - distance from the city center / 2. This is the 2: how fast value falls as you move away from the middle. Because the rule is written this way, no city the engine produces has two centers, and no place far from the middle can be expensive. Raising the divisor flattens the gradient, so the city gets richer and less centralised, but it still has one center.

max_traffic_distance.title: How far traffic looks
max_traffic_distance.description: A zone counts as having access to jobs if a random walk along the roads finds a destination within this many steps. There's no route planning, no journey time and no congestion feeding back; the walk is random and the only question is whether it arrives. On a compact grid like the starting city most destinations are close, so this control does less here than it would on a sprawling map.

smooth_passes.title: Police smoothing passes
smooth_passes.description: How a police station's influence spreads: the map of station positions is blurred this many times and the result is called coverage. That is the whole account of how a service reaches a neighborhood. At 0, cover collapses to the stations themselves and crime rises everywhere else.

birth_rate.title: Birth rate
birth_rate.description: Population growth per turn, as a flat share of the residential population. There are no ages, no households and no migration; demography in this model is one multiplication.

ext_market_index.title: Outside demand
ext_market_index.description: Demand for what the city's industry produces, from everywhere that isn't the city. In the game it's one of three numbers set by the difficulty level, and it never changes for any other reason.

seed.title: Seed
seed.description: The starting number for every random choice the simulation makes. The rules and the starting city are the same for every seed, so this is the only thing that differs between the runs on the divergence chart. A different seed gives a different city out of the same model.

run_count.title: Runs to compare
run_count.description: How many seeds the divergence chart runs in the background. Each starts from the same city under the same rules. The spread between them at the end is how much the rules leave to chance.

ticks.title: Steps per run
ticks.description: How many steps each comparison run takes. One step is one phase of the sixteen-phase cycle, so a full turn of the city's clock is sixteen steps.
